newsitem.title: MONGOLIA: Mongolian fuel prices soar since prices freed.
newsitem.headline: Mongolian fuel prices soar since prices freed.

text.p: Mongolian fuel prices have risen as much as 80.1 percent since they were freed in early September, oil company officials said on Wednesday.

Officials of Neft Import Concern, the state-controlled oil importer and distributor, said price increases ranged from 43.1 percent to 80.1 percent during the period and were due largely to weakness in the Mongolian currency.
Mongolia, which imports all of its oil, freed its energy prices in September to bring domestic prices in the cash-strapped nation closer to world levels.
The state had been losing money on imported oil, most of it bought from Russia.
The biggest price rise has been in the remote, far western region of Mongolia where 76 octane petrol rose 80.1 percent to 227 tugriks ($0.33) per litre from 126 tugriks in September.
Diesel fuel in the western region climbed 74 percent to 262 tugriks per litre, while 93 octane gasoline rose 60 percent to 263 tugriks.
In the capital, Ulan Bator, the price of 93 octane gasoline rose 43.1 percent to 235 tugriks, while 76 octane petrol gained 59 percent to 200 tugriks and diesel was up 57 percent to 237 tugriks.
Neft accounts for most of the oil market in Mongolia. ($1 = 690 tugriks)
